name: Box
summary: This guide explains how to set up your own OAuth 2.0 application for Box, providing secure delegated access for your users. You will use Box's Developer Console to create and configure your user app, assign the required redirect URI, set appropriate scopes, and—if your users are part of certain Box enterprises—may need an enterprise admin to explicitly allow your unpublished app. A managed public marketplace app is not required for integration or for most production use cases.
decision: Follow the path to create your own Box OAuth 2.0 app in the Box Developer Console, add your integration's redirect URI, configure scopes, and use your client credentials. You only need Box administrator involvement if your customer's enterprise has unpublished apps disabled by default. There is no approval or review required from Box unless you intend to publish the app to the marketplace.

prerequisites.title: Box Account with Developer Console access
prerequisites.body: A Box account is required. A free developer account is sufficient to create and manage OAuth apps.

steps.title: Log into Box Developer Console
steps.body: Go to https://app.box.com/developers/console and sign in with your Box account.

steps.title: Create a new custom OAuth app
steps.body: Choose 'New App', select 'Custom App', provide a name, description, and purpose (e.g., 'Integration' and 'Workflow'), then select 'OAuth 2.0' as authentication and click Create.
steps.note: 'User' app type is synonymous with 'Custom App' for OAuth 2.0 as per Box documentation.

steps.title: Set application scopes
steps.body: Select the minimum scopes your integration requires, e.g., 'Read all files and folders stored in Box' or 'Read and write all files and folders stored in Box'. Click Save.
steps.note: Read and write encompasses read; pick only what's necessary.

steps.title: Configure CORS domains (if needed)
steps.body: If your integration makes direct browser API calls, add your application's origin to the 'CORS Domain' allow-list. If it's server-to-server, you can skip this.

steps.title: Copy client ID and client secret
steps.body: After creation, locate and securely store your app's OAuth 2.0 credentials: Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.note: Store these securely for use in your integration.

steps.title: Test your OAuth integration
steps.body: Initiate an OAuth authorization flow to ensure configuration is correct. Log in, approve requested permissions, and verify the connection.

blockers.title: Enterprise admin approval (conditional)
blockers.body: If your customer's Box enterprise has 'Disable unpublished apps by default' enabled, a Box admin must approve your app by its client ID before users can connect.
blockers.note: This is rare; applies only if enterprise toggles that setting.

human_actions.title: Log into Box Developer Console
human_actions.body: A person must manually sign in and perform app creation and configuration steps.

human_actions.title: Input redirect URI and scopes
human_actions.body: A human must specify the correct redirect URI and select the required scopes; this cannot be auto-configured.

human_actions.title: Copy application credentials securely
human_actions.body: Client ID and secret need to be retrieved and set in the connector or integration's configuration.

human_actions.title: Consent to permissions during OAuth flow
human_actions.body: The end user must authenticate and approve requested access when first connecting.
